findings.location: AD-PSI-7 Canonical identity and replay (line 305), Project Structure and Ownership (lines 475-478), and exact-owner self-review (line 633)
findings.affected_requirement: The approved proposal section 3 and August architecture section 4.1 require the semantic symbol to remain bound through the Pass 1 Worker packet; FR-084 and SC-029 require the resulting Pass 1 Document and current Source Anchor to be integrity-bound to the reviewed owner.
findings.evidence: The plan states that the existing Worker packet already consumes CodeUnit.SymbolName and therefore omits the prepared Pass 1 packet contract from its implementation surface. Raw source contradicts this: both PreparedPass1FileCodeUnitAssignment and PreparedPass1WorkerPacket in src/dotnet/Vulgata.Core/DomainServices/IPreparedPass1WorkerDispatcher.cs carry RepositoryRelativePath and range fields but no SymbolName; PreparedPass1ClaimedPacketSource constructs the packet without SymbolName, and the prepared dispatcher likewise cannot validate or carry it. The proposed repository/handoff identity checks do not close this accepted packet-boundary requirement.
findings.correction_outcome: Revise AD-PSI-7, the ownership table, contracts, data model, and test matrix to define the exact prepared Pass 1 symbol projection. Include the necessary Core packet/assignment contract and producing/consuming seams, require server-side revalidation of SymbolName against the v1/v2 identity before dispatch and after re-fetch, and add behavioral tests proving the semantic symbol reaches the prepared Worker packet while path-valued units retain their exact prior packet behavior. Keep provider-visible prompt/tool behavior unchanged unless a separately authorized need is proven.

findings.location: AD-PSI-7 JDT evidence decision (line 294), Infrastructure ownership (line 477), and exact-owner feasibility self-review (line 633)
findings.affected_requirement: The approved decision and August architecture section 4.1 require exactly one current same-path JDT-LS top-level Type whose reported name and exact UTF-16 range validate the profile FQN and selector line; neither profile data nor untyped symbol evidence may establish the binding alone.
findings.evidence: The plan assumes AnalysisSymbolEvidence.Kind is trustworthy JDT Type evidence and limits production work to PreparedJavaRangeSource. In current source, JdtLsAnalysisAdapter.ParseEvidence does not read the LSP document-symbol kind at all: it constructs every returned item with AnalysisSymbolKind.Type. Consequently, filtering for AnalysisSymbolKind.Type in PreparedJavaRangeSource cannot distinguish a class/interface/enum/record from another document-symbol kind, and fake range-source tests cannot prove the real production adapter supplies the required Type authority. The plan also excludes JdtLsAnalysisAdapter from its ownership and protocol-test seams, leaving the central two-authority decision unproven.
findings.correction_outcome: Revise AD-PSI-7 and ownership/test sections to establish a real typed document-symbol boundary. Either include a bounded documentSymbol-specific JdtLsAnalysisAdapter projection that validates supported LSP Type kinds, top-level response shape, exact name/path/range and rejects unsupported or malformed kinds, with protocol-level tests, or identify and prove an existing equally authoritative typed seam. Preserve unrelated navigation behavior and retain fail-closed handling before Manifest publication.

summary: REVISE. AD-PSI-7 is the correct earliest plan owner and the v1/v2 identity, UTF-16 ownership, transaction, replay, failure, nonmatching compatibility, no-migration, and PostgreSQL vertical concepts are otherwise coherent. However, the plan relies on two source capabilities that do not exist: the prepared Pass 1 packet has no SymbolName, and the JDT adapter synthesizes Type for every document-symbol item instead of preserving actual typed evidence. These are load-bearing authority and feasibility gaps, so task generation and planned-change authorization must wait for a corrected plan and a fresh independent plan review. The AGENTS.md Scan planned-change trigger remains active; no Worker Agent tool or PRD/security weakening is proposed by this verdict. The unrelated user-owned .env.example was excluded from the reviewed boundary, and git diff --check passed for all five owned plan paths.
